_comment: CANONICAL contract for the Sentry PII scrub. tubermed-web/lib/sentry-scrub.ts and tubermed-backend/lib/sentry-scrub.js are two independent implementations of THIS document; each repo's own gate executes its implementation against it, and tubermed-backend/scripts/verify-mirror.js byte-compares its copy against this one. That composition is what makes 'the two scrubbers agree' a checked fact instead of a comment. Do NOT let an implementation read this file — an implementation that reads its own spec agrees with it by construction.
why: This is a medical product handling special-category data. An error payload must never carry a transcript, a request body, credentials, identity, or console context. sendDefaultPii:false prevents most of it; this contract makes it a guarantee.
_floor_warning: A refuter deleted entries from BOTH copies of this file and from the web implementation only: the copies stayed byte-identical, verify-mirror stayed green, and the web gate — which is contract-driven — weakened in lockstep with the spec it was checking. Each gate therefore carries its OWN hardcoded minimum set of channels, written in the gate source, and fails if this file drops below it. Mirroring proves the two specs are IDENTICAL; it can never prove either is STRONG.

url.why: On the browser SDK path query_string is never emitted at all — the query lives INSIDE request.url. What rides there: ?visit=<consultation uuid>, ?q=<free-text admin search>, and ?session=<sessionId>, which is the phone-upload credential. Deleting query_string and leaving request.url alone closed a channel that was never open and left the one that was.
url.policy_why: origin_and_pathname (version 2) kept every path segment, and the same two identifiers travel as path params as well as query params: /api/sessions/:id IS the phone-upload credential, and thirteen /api/consultations/:id/... routes carry the consultation uuid. Origin-only would destroy route-level triage, which is most of what Sentry is for. route_shape keeps the route and loses the identifiers.

by_shape.hex_token: a segment of 8 or more characters, all of them [0-9a-f] case-insensitive — the phone session id is crypto.randomBytes(6).toString('hex'), always 12
by_shape.digits: a segment of one or more characters, all [0-9]

by_position.why: Shape rules cannot catch a short or unusually-formed identifier, and the segment after a collection name IS an identifier by construction. The direction of a mistake here is to redact a route literal, which costs triage detail; the direction of a missing rule is to publish a credential. The literal list is deliberately tiny — anything not on it is treated as an id.

message.redacted_to: [redacted: message not on the tag allowlist]
message.why: lib/usage-caps.js calls Sentry.captureMessage today, so 'assert it empty' is not available — the assertion would be false on the first cap crossing. It is scrubbed instead. Only a message whose first token is an allowed bracketed tag survives; anything else is replaced wholesale, so a captureMessage added later carries nothing until its tag is added here deliberately. logentry.params is ALWAYS dropped: it holds interpolation values, which is exactly where a caller would put the variable part.
message.policy_why: The commit that dropped breadcrumbs argued that a no-PII guarantee resting on every caller's discipline is not a guarantee. That argument applies here identically: message was safe only because the one caller happened to build its string from a closed enum and two counts.

known_residuals.unscrubbed_event_fields: This contract now governs request/user/breadcrumbs/extra/contexts, request.url and message/logentry. Still neither deleted nor asserted: tags, transaction, server_name, fingerprint, threads, spans and debug_meta. Safe by discipline, not by construction. Nothing writes to them today in either repo. RULING OWED.
known_residuals.encoded_query: A query encoded into the path (%3F) stays in pathname by definition, so it survives route_shape unless the encoded remainder happens to match a segment rule. Narrow: it needs a caller that percent-encodes a '?' into a path, and no code in either repo builds a URL that way.

keep_why: The exception message and stack are what actually fix bugs, and they are verified non-PII (fixed literals / API strings). The method is a bare verb.
